Subject: Acropolis SLA amendment & credit bands — initial ask

Hi Lisa / Acropolis procurement team,

Thanks again for the time last week. As we dig into the procurement checklist you sent over, I wanted to surface a proposed narrow SLA amendment that would cover the regulated inference endpoints you described. Your ask was essentially: a firm uptime commitment, tighter latency SLOs for clinical inference, and a clearly defined monthly credit schedule for any availability/latency shortfalls.

Quick summary of what you asked:
- Baseline uptime target: 99.99% for clinical endpoints (higher than our default template)
- Latency P95 target for inference calls: ~150ms
- No more than 1x monthly credit cap and straightforward payout mechanics

To keep procurement moving, can you confirm which of these are absolute requirements versus preferences? If 99.99% is a hard regulatory requirement, that will require changes to our deployment topology (cross-region redundancy for dedicated pools) and a tailored credit cap.

I’m attaching a draft amendment with two options — one closer to our standard template (Option A) and a stricter, higher-commitment option (Option B) that includes a higher credit floor and explicit cross-region failover. I’ve also pulled together an action plan and will loop in legal/finance if you want to move Option B forward.

Attachments: Proposed_SLA_Amendment_v2.pdf (summary of Option A/B) and Acropolis_Mutual_Action_Plan.xlsx (timeline).

Next steps: please indicate preference A or B, and any non-negotiable points (credit cap, audit evidence, retreat-of-liability). Happy to jump on a brief call to walk through tradeoffs.

Thanks,

Connor —

Appreciate the quick follow. A few clarifications from our side:
- 99.99% is our target for production clinical inference used in decision support. It is driven by internal risk assessments; anything below that triggers escalation to our compliance board.
- Latency: P95 150ms is preferred, but P95 <= 250ms is acceptable for now if paired with clear mitigation and a credit schedule for repeated breaches.
- Credit cap: we can accept a cap but we need the cap to be meaningful (ideally at least the equivalent of one month of fees for a severe availability breach).
- Audit evidence: we require monthly availability reports, detailed incident timelines, and access to relevant logs (redacted as needed).

If Option B requires additional infra (cross-region), we need an estimate of the timeline and any upfront costs or lead times. Also, can you confirm the maximum monthly credit cap you would accept and whether it’s capped at a percent of spend or a fixed dollar amount?

We’d like to see a concrete counterproposal that maps availability bands to credit percentages and includes a latency-band mapping — that will help us take it to our legal/procurement review.

Thanks,
Lisa Thompson
Director of IT Operations
Acropolis Health

From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>

Date: Thu, 11 Dec 2026 14:50:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Acropolis SLA amendment & credit bands — counterproposal draft (internal)

Forwarding Lisa's note — Acropolis wants a mapped availability->credit schedule and is asking if 99.99% is non-negotiable. They said P95 250ms is acceptable if paired with mitigation and credits.

My suggested counter (to review):
- Standard template remains at 99.95% uptime. For Acropolis (regulated clinical): offer a tailored amendment with the following graduated monthly credit bands (availability measured monthly, monthly invoice as baseline):
  - >= 99.95% — no credit (meets target)
  - >= 99.90% and < 99.95% — 10% of monthly service fee credit
  - >= 99.50% and < 99.90% — 30% credit
  - < 99.50% — 60% credit (severe availability failure)
- Cap: legal recommends a cap of 3x the monthly service fee or one quarter of annual committed spend, whichever is lower. Proposal: cap = 3x monthly fee.
- Latency (P95) exceptions: standard P95 150ms, but for Acropolis amend to P95 250ms with the following credit matrix if P95 exceeds thresholds for more than two business days in a month:
  - P95 between 150ms–250ms: monitoring + remediation, no credit for a single occurrence; credits only if persistent (>48 hours)
  - P95 between 250ms–400ms for >48 hours: 10% credit
  - P95 >400ms for >48 hours: 25% credit (service-impacting)
- Audit & reporting: monthly availability report, incident postmortem within 5 business days for any credit-triggering event, and access to aggregated audit logs via secure link.
- Cross-region failover: Option B (higher commitment) requires dedicated cross-region reserve capacity. Estimate: 6–8 weeks to provision plus integration testing; potential for modest incremental monthly charge (TBD).

Legal/finance notes (Ben): keep the cap and exclude force majeure and scheduled maintenance (with proper notice). Operational (Stephanie): need to confirm that the KV cache & prefix caching behavior will not affect the P95 numbers for clinical traffic; we may want to carve out cold-start penalties in month 1 of rollout.

Can you each reply with redlines or a green light and I’ll package for a customer-facing amendment.

—Connor

Lisa / procurement team —

Thanks for the detail and patience while we reviewed internally. Attached is a customer-facing draft (Proposed_SLA_Amendment_v2.pdf) and a short mutual action plan (Acropolis_Mutual_Action_Plan.xlsx). Key points of the amendment (Option B-lite) we are proposing based on your ask and internal guardrails:

Availability (monthly measurement):
- Baseline (tailored) target: 99.95% uptime (we are not able to guarantee 99.99% without a dedicated cross-region deployment).
- Credit bands:
  - >= 99.95% — no credit
  - >= 99.90% and < 99.95% — 10% credit of monthly invoice
  - >= 99.50% and < 99.90% — 30% credit of monthly invoice
  - < 99.50% — 60% credit of monthly invoice
- Cap: credit payments capped at 3x the monthly invoice (legal-compliant cap).

Latency (P95) — clinical inference endpoints (tailored):
- Operational target: P95 <= 250ms
- Credit triggers (persistent breaches >48 hours):
  - 250ms–400ms: 10% credit
  - >400ms: 25% credit
- Single-day spikes below these thresholds will trigger investigation and technical mitigation but do not immediately result in credits.

Reporting & evidence:
- Monthly availability report published to secure link
- Incident timeline and a root-cause postmortem within 5 business days for any credit-triggering event
- Aggregated, redacted logs available on request for audits

Operational notes:
- Option to upgrade to full cross-region dedicated pools (to approach 99.99%) — estimated 6–8 weeks and a separate procurement path for dedicated reserves. We’ve documented the timeline in the attached MAP.

Next steps: please review the attached amendment and indicate acceptance of Option B-lite, or flag specific redlines. If you accept, we will route the amendment to DocuSign and begin the provisioning checklist. If you want the 99.99% commitment, I can put together a costed plan for cross-region dedicated capacity.

Attachments: Proposed_SLA_Amendment_v2.pdf, Acropolis_Mutual_Action_Plan.xlsx

Thanks,
